Wrap the official dsh web UI into a native-feeling, always-on desktop app. / 为 DeepSeek Harness（"},{"id":"p1s3","text":"DeepSeek 开源的可插拔 AI agent harness）打造的桌面应用壳，把官方 dsh web 界面包装成原生质感、常驻后台的桌面应用。"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# DeepSeek Harness Desktop"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"English | 简体中文"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"> [!WARNING]
> **Maintenance mode.** As of 2026-09-29 this project is no longer developed: no new fe"},{"id":"p4s2","text":"atures, and no tracking of upstream dsh releases. The official DeepSeek Harness desktop app (<https:"},{"id":"p4s3","text":"//www.deepseek.com/download/>) is the recommended replacement on Windows x64 and Apple-silicon macOS"},{"id":"p4s4","text":". The last shell release, v1.3.2, and every earlier build stay available on the Releases page indefi"},{"id":"p4s5","text":"nitely, and the MIT license means you are free to fork it.

Adaptation fixes only: no timeline, no feature requests."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"A desktop shell for DeepSeek Harness — the pluggable AI agent harness from DeepSeek. Wrap the offici"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"al `dsh web` UI into a native-feeling, always-on desktop app, **reusing the `dsh` CLI you already ha"},{"id":"p5s3","text":"sh web` UI into a native-feeling, always-on desktop app, **reusing the `dsh` CLI you already have**."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"## Features"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"### Recovery Center — when an update breaks the backend"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"dsh moves fast and occasionally ships breaking changes, and plugins often lag behind — so a dsh upda"},{"id":"p8s2","text":"te can leave the backend unable to boot, and a plugin that used to work can suddenly take the whole "},{"id":"p8s3","text":"harness down with it. Until now, all the shell told you was a dead-end "backend exited unexpectedly""},{"id":"p8s4","text":" dialog: no plugin name, no error detail, no way to fix anything in place."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"The Recovery Center is the shell's answer — a native page that turns a broken backend into a few cli"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"Recovery Center is the shell's answer — a native page that turns a broken backend into a few clicks:"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"- **Automatic on failure** — when dsh crashes or fails to boot, the shell switches to the Recovery C"},{"id":"p10s2","text":"enter by itself: a rolling output snapshot (token-redacted) plus an automatic diagnosis that pinpoin"},{"id":"p10s3","text":"ts the failing plugin when dsh names one, falling back to a plain "here's the log" when it can't
- *"},{"id":"p10s4","text":"*Plugin rescue** — disable/enable writes the profile patch layer with whole-file validation and atom"},{"id":"p10s5","text":"ic replacement (it will never corrupt your hand-edited lines or leave the backend unbootable); unins"},{"id":"p10s6","text":"tall/update runs the `dsh plugin` CLI with live logs. Host-critical modules are protected and refuse"},{"id":"p10s7","text":" to be touched
- **Version switching, unified** — upgrade and rollback share one list (npm global an"},{"id":"p10s8","text":"d git source, channel badges, current version pinned on top), with live progress and an automatic re"},{"id":"p10s9","text":"start back to the normal page when done
- **Single entry** — version maintenance lives here even whe"},{"id":"p10s10","text":"n everything is fine: Settings → Desktop checks for updates, and confirming an update hands off to t"},{"id":"p10s11","text":"he Recovery Center (no scary diagnostics, just progress) — no terminal needed, ever"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"### Backend (dsh) integration"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"- **Dual backend sources** — run the `dsh` from your npm global install (stable channel) or from a l"},{"id":"p12s2","text":"ocal git checkout (any version, including pre-releases), switchable in Settings. `Auto` mode prefers"},{"id":"p12s3","text":" npm and falls back to the source directory; if the chosen source breaks, the shell falls back to th"},{"id":"p12s4","text":"e other one and tells you why
- **Zero-intrusion wrapper** — spawns the chosen `dsh` as a child proc"},{"id":"p12s5","text":"ess (`dsh web`), loads its localhost UI; the harness source is never modified. One dsh shared by ter"},{"id":"p12s6","text":"minal and desktop — plugins, settings, credentials, sessions and versions always match (`DSH_HOME`, "},{"id":"p12s7","text":"default `~/.dsh`)
- **Source mode without terminals** — pick a folder and the shell drives everythin"},{"id":"p12s8","text":"g: clone the official repo, run `pnpm install` + `pnpm build` with live logs, validate the result, t"},{"id":"p12s9","text":"hen boot. The only prerequisites are `git` and `pnpm` on PATH
- **Source-mode updates without termin"},{"id":"p12s10","text":"als either** — the shell checks the upstream tags, then one click checks out the chosen version, rei"},{"id":"p12s11","text":"nstalls, rebuilds and restarts the backend — the same pipeline the Recovery Center drives, just reac"},{"id":"p12s12","text":"hed from Settings. Dirty worktrees are refused with a clear message
- **One proxy for every update c"},{"id":"p12s13","text":"hannel** — a single proxy setting covers git (clone/fetch), pnpm (install/build) and npm (check/upgr"},{"id":"p12s14","text":"ade); git uses per-invocation config, never touching your global gitconfig
- **First-run setup page*"},{"id":"p12s15","text":"* — no dsh detected? The app offers a copyable install command, a one-click in-app install, or the s"},{"id":"p12s16","text":"ource-mode path (clone + prepare), then boots automatically"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"### Prerequisites"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"- **npm channel (default)**: Node.js ≥ 22 and the `dsh` CLI (`npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh`) — if missi"},{"id":"p14s2","text":"ng, the app shows a setup page with a copyable command or a one-click in-app install
- **Source chan"},{"id":"p14s3","text":"nel (optional)**: additionally requires `git` and `pnpm` on PATH; the shell clones the repo and runs"},{"id":"p14s4","text":" `pnpm install` + `pnpm build` for you — supported dsh versions (≥ 0.1.5-rc.1) use the prebuilt `nod"},{"id":"p14s5","text":"e-addon-system`, so **no C++ build toolchain is needed** (historical 0.1.3.x compiled `fs-ext` and i"},{"id":"p14s6","text":"s outside the supported range)"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"## Known limitations (v1.x)"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"- Requires Node.js ≥ 22 and **dsh ≥ 0.1.5-rc.1**; the npm channel needs a globally-installed `dsh` C"},{"id":"p16s2","text":"LI (the setup page offers one-click install), the source channel needs `git` + `pnpm` — the shell bu"},{"id":"p16s3","text":"ndles no runtime either way, so the installer stays small. Older dsh versions need an older shell re"},{"id":"p16s4","text":"lease (see the dsh version support table above)
- macOS builds are unsigned — Gatekeeper requires ri"},{"id":"p16s5","text":"ght-click → Open on first run; macOS has no auto-update (needs a signing certificate)
- Windows auto"},{"id":"p16s6","text":"-update is guided (downloads then runs the installer) rather than silent, due to the unsigned build
"},{"id":"p16s7","text":"- The source channel checks out release tags in detached HEAD — switch your branch back manually if "},{"id":"p16s8","text":"you develop in the same clone
- **Known unfixed issue**: if the shell exits abnormally, the `dsh` ch"},{"id":"p16s9","text":"ild it spawned can survive as an orphan and keep holding the fixed port, so the next launch falls ba"},{"id":"p16s10","text":"ck to a random port. Workaround: stop the leftover `dsh web` process (Windows: `taskkill /F /PID <pi"},{"id":"p16s11","text":"d>`), then relaunch — the port returns to `3080`."}],"truncated":true}
